clue.text: Is it sex results from this? Time for more freedom!

parts.words: Is it sex results from this
parts.note: read the answer as an instruction: the second word, with the first as an anagram signal, has its letters swung about to give the clue's opening three words

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about whether liberated sex was the product of a permissive decade.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: taking 'swinging' as an anagram indicator, the letters of SIXTIES rearrange to IS IT SEX, the clue's own opening words.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1960s are remembered as the decade of social and sexual liberation, a period of new freedoms.

clue.text: One Greek character in match least able to stand up straight?

definitions.text: least able to stand up straight?

indicators.note: the first pieces are placed in the middle of the word for the match

parts.note: a test match is an international cricket match
one is I, the Roman numeral
psi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A sports fan at a match who has had the most to drink and is wobbling.
explanation.walkthrough: TEST is a test match, an international cricket fixture lasting several days.
explanation.definitionFit: The most drunk person is the one least able to stand steadily, a jokey description.

clue.text: Old boundary within home territory

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words home territory, spanning the gap

explanation.surface: An ancient border line lying inside one's own land.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun this is an archaic word for a boundary or limit, as in 'metes and bounds'.

clue.text: See plant getting protected in wind

indicators.note: the plant is shielded by being enclosed within the letters of the see

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese; Ely is a cathedral city and see in Cambridgeshire
an aster is a daisy-like flowering plant

explanation.surface: A flower being sheltered from the wind in a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England, so a 'see' in crosswordese.
explanation.definitionFit: A wind blowing from the east is called by this name, used as a noun.

clue.text: Put in gym, daughter had fun

indicators.note: the word for put goes inside the letters for gym

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school gym class
to lay something is to put it down

explanation.surface: A girl sent to the gym who enjoyed herself.
explanation.definitionFit: To amuse oneself in games is to have fun, the past tense matching 'had'.

clue.text: In storm one needs a support

indicators.note: the single letter a is placed inside the word for storm

parts.note: to bluster is to rage or storm about noisily

explanation.surface: During a gale, everyone needs something sturdy to grip.
explanation.definitionFit: A baluster is one of the short posts holding up a handrail, so a type of support.

clue.text: Duck has suffered on island

indicators.note: the duck is placed on the end of the word for suffered

parts.note: borne means endured or suffered
a duck is a zero score in cricket, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A duck that has had a bad time on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a score of nought in cricket, hence O.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large island in South-East Asia, shared by three nations.

clue.text: Senior academic, awful gossiper for sure

indicators.note: something awful is in a dreadful state, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A distinguished professor who is certainly a dreadful tittle-tattle.
explanation.definitionFit: A Regius chair is a professorship founded by the Crown, among the most senior posts at old British universities.

clue.text: Civil service barrier restricts success, what?

indicators.note: the barrier holds the other letters confined within it

parts.note: a wall is a barrier
a hit is a success
eh? is a request to repeat, meaning what?

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about bureaucracy blocking achievement.
explanation.definitionFit: Whitehall, the London street of government ministries, stands by metonymy for the British civil service.

clue.text: A flower sprang up

parts.note: a rose is a flower

explanation.surface: A bloom that shot up quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are past tense verbs meaning came upward, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Was one badly troubled initially? Not a problem!

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so these letters are rearranged
only the opening letter of troubled is taken

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a person was upset, and is told it was fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges WASONE to NOSWEA; 'initially' adds T.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an informal idiom for something easy, posing no difficulty.

clue.text: We can be heard as two characters in quiz

indicators.note: spoken, the letter names sound like a phrase

parts.note: the two inner letters of quiz are U and I

explanation.surface: A quiz pairing presented as a team.
explanation.walkthrough: Saying the letters U and I, from inside 'quiz', gives the pronouns.
explanation.definitionFit: The first person plural pronoun covers the speaker plus the listener.

clue.text: Holly perhaps as one left with lover no longer

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: Someone named Holly left alone after a break-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holly' looks like a woman's name; it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilex is the botanical genus of hollies, so holly is an example.

clue.text: Trains a dog awkwardly to make steps

indicators.note: done awkwardly means clumsily, so the letters come out disordered

explanation.surface: Someone clumsily training a dog to climb stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Gradations are stages in a series, small incremental degrees of change.

clue.text: Criminal escape that sounds unbelievable!

definitions.meaning: a fleeing by robbers after a crime
'...!' is an exclamation of disbelief, as if to say that is incredible

explanation.surface: A robbers' flight so daring it seems incredible.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a criminals' escape; spoken as two words it expresses amazement.

clue.text: Betting syndicate going after money after work?

indicators.note: the syndicate is placed following the word for pay

parts.note: a wage is money earned for work
a ring is a cartel or syndicate

explanation.surface: A gambling syndicate going after people's pay packets.
explanation.definitionFit: To wager is to bet, so wagering means placing bets.

clue.text: Citizen's fast food, hard to eat

indicators.note: the food swallows a letter, taking it inside

parts.note: a burger is fast food
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A city dweller's burger that is tough to chew.
explanation.definitionFit: A burgher is a freeman of a town, a citizen of a borough.

clue.text: Force through pretentious nonsense, then rest

indicators.note: then signals that one piece follows the other

parts.note: bull is empty, pompous talk
to doze is to rest

explanation.surface: Pushing through pompous rubbish, then taking a nap.
explanation.definitionFit: To bulldoze a measure is to push it through regardless of opposition.

clue.text: Valiant rendition of symphony in empty hall

indicators.note: the symphony goes inside the remaining letters
emptying the word leaves just its first and last letters

parts.note: the Eroica is Beethoven's Third Symphony

explanation.surface: A brave performance of a symphony to a deserted hall.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an archaic variant meaning brave or heroic, so valiant fits.

clue.text: Sheep coming together by home as a complete unit?

parts.note: in means at home
a teg is a sheep in its second year
a rally is a gathering

explanation.surface: A flock gathering by the farmhouse as one.
explanation.walkthrough: A teg is a two-year-old sheep, an old farming word.
explanation.definitionFit: Integrally means as an essential whole, describing parts forming one entity.

clue.text: Partner lacking energy tucked into excessive salad food

indicators.note: the partner is inserted within the word for excessive

parts.note: too means excessively

indicators.note: the partner is without the energy letter

parts.note: a mate is a partner
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A tired partner tucking into far too much salad.
explanation.definitionFit: This red fruit is a staple ingredient of salads.

clue.text: Inclined to upset pals, one being heartless

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are disturbed
removing the middle leaves only the outside letters of one

explanation.surface: Someone tempted to annoy friends, being unkind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being heartless' cuts one to OE; 'upset' rearranges PALS with OE.
explanation.definitionFit: Aslope means sloping, at an angle, so tilted or inclined.

clue.text: It takes endless hard work to produce a tennis champion

indicators.note: endless means losing the final letter

parts.note: graft is hard work

explanation.surface: Becoming a tennis champion requires relentless effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Steffi Graf won 22 Grand Slam singles titles.

clue.text: Last three bits of glass thrown back in cart

indicators.note: the reversal applies only to the final three letters
thrown back means turned the other way round

parts.note: a tumbler is a drinking glass

explanation.surface: Someone throwing back the last of their glasses of wine while seated in a cart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last three bits of ... thrown back' turns LER at the end of TUMBLER into REL.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumbrel is a two-wheeled farm cart, famous for taking victims to the guillotine.

clue.text: Final military order received — is mission pared down?

indicators.note: final means the last letter of the word received is taken
pared down means trimmed, losing its ending

explanation.surface: A soldier receiving the last command and wondering if the operation has been scaled back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Final' takes D from received; 'pared down' cuts mission to MISS.
explanation.definitionFit: On parade, the command to end a formation and release troops is shouted as this word.

clue.text: Drink spirits initially, something that goes to the head

indicators.note: only the opening letter of spirits is taken

parts.words: something that goes to the head
parts.note: a wig is worn on the head

explanation.surface: Spirits are a drink that quickly goes to one's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'something that goes to the head' suggests drunkenness but is a wig.
explanation.definitionFit: A swig is a large gulp of a beverage.

clue.text: The foreign fashion revealed by a singing John

parts.note: el is 'the' in Spanish
ton means fashion or style

explanation.surface: A foreign fashion displayed by a vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: Elton John is the British pop star, so his first name is the singing John.

clue.text: Mostly Italian food given to one pet? Nothing to be plucked

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: pizza is Italian food
I is the Roman numeral for one
a cat is a pet
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Feeding Italian food to a pet, which then needs plucking.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction telling string players to pluck rather than bow.
